To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
caveolin-1 interacts with EphB1 and regulates its membrane targeting and activation.

EphB1 and EphA2 receptors localize to caveolae and directly interact with the scaffolding domain of caveolin- 1 upon ligand activation, and that caveolin binding to EphB1 is necessary for its correct membrane localization and downstream signaling.
EphB1 is a caveolar protein, that EphB1 and EphA2 interact with caveolin, and that this interaction is important for membrane localization and signaling of EphB1 receptors.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of EphB1 in the control of angiogenesis and the identification of caveolin- 1 as an important regulatory factor for this process.
the role of Eph receptors in angiogenesis, a process that is crucial for the growth and development of the embryo and the maintenance of the adult organism.
the role of Eph receptors and their ligands, the ephrins, in vascular development and angiogenesis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Ephs are localized in caveolar micro-domains, and their signaling and membrane targeting is regulated by caveolin- 1.
EphB1 is regulated by caveolin- 1, a protein that has been shown previously to regulate the function of several other signaling molecules.
the caveolar localization of Ephs is a prerequisite for Eph-mediated activation of ERK.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
EphB1 receptor is a new member of the growing list of proteins regulated by caveolin- 1.
caveolin-1 regulates EphB1 receptor localization and signaling in caveolae.
EphB1 and EphA2 are localized in caveolar microdomains where they interact with caveolin and where they are activated by ephrin ligands.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the interaction between EphB1 and caveolin- 1 regulates EphB1 signaling.
the interaction of EphB1 with caveolin- 1, and thus its localization to caveolar microdomains, is important for its activation of downstream signaling.
caveolin-1 not only regulates EphB1-mediated signaling but also plays a role in the targeting of EphB to the plasma membrane.
